reviews.title: Article content doesn’t load on iOS 27
reviews.text: Tapping on an article in the app fails to load the content, I’m forced to load in the browser

reviews.title: Anti-trust or incompetence?
reviews.text: I should be able to login to this app with any credentials I used to purchase my WSJ subscription. Instead, Apple only wants me to login with my Apple account ID. To do this, I would have to purchase another sub through Apple. That would seem too stupid to be done on purpose, so maybe it’s simply incompetence. Either way, it needs to be fixed!

reviews.title: Horrible update to iPad app
reviews.text: Can no longer read downloaded print edition or saved articles offline. I want to be able to read articles even when there is no WiFi

reviews.title: Fluff pieces as breaking news notifications
reviews.text: Breaking news notifications should be just that, and only that. I don’t want notifications for fluff pieces.

reviews.title: App shows WSJ articles incorrectly
reviews.text:
Lately the app consistently drops sections of articles, usually cutting off a paragraph halfway and then picking up the next paragraph as if nothing happened. The web version of the WSJ works fine for the same articles so this is an app failure.

Is anyone at WSJ actually testing this thing?  Or are you all too focused on adding more video ads to check if your app works for, you know, reading the newspaper?

reviews.title: No more offline access to saved articles
reviews.text: This app has always been marginal, at best, given the subscription price. The latest app update is the final straw for me. Suddenly, I can’t read my saved articles while I’m offline. This defeats the entire purpose of saving articles!!! Any frequent flier will tell you that airplane WiFi isn’t always working. If I can’t access my articles without a signal, there’s no point in having the app. Or a subscription. I’m out.

reviews.title: Latest Release 15.12.1
reviews.text:
Reading the article on wind turbines and the app has crashed both times, once requiring the iPad to be power cycled.
The app has always had its issues but this is unacceptable. Giving up on the app and maybe my subscription if it doesn’t get any better. 
Unfortunate since the WSJ is some of the best unbiased reporting.

reviews.title: Woke yuppie tabloid
reviews.text:
Weak shadow of once great paper.

Woke US coverage.  Chatty pieces on fashions and McMansions.

Bookmark function in the app often fails.

reviews.title: Where are the comments?
reviews.text: Why aren’t you able to see comments or make comments on the articles within the app, like online?   Enable this feature and I’ll switch to the app.

reviews.title: Breaking News Notifications
reviews.text:
Recently I started receiving notifications of non-breaking news stories. The reason? The notification setting to turn on “Breaking News” is described as “Breaking news, important developments and other stories we think you might like.”

Don’t group these…

reviews.title: Dumb notifications
reviews.text: Being financial app, the notifications are awful

reviews.title: Why can’t the WSJ get subscriber access straight?!?!?!
reviews.text:
For years, off and on, I’ve had the print and digital editions of the WSJ.
I may know the bill is paid,
and how to sign in ( and out), but no matter what
I do— or don’t do— I can be reading a book review
or an editorial, and the “ dreaded fade-out” begins, as ALWAYS ACCOMPANIED by the satanic message: You are reading your last FREE article.
This is then folowed by a jeremiad of subscription offers, and all the while, the ingongerous “Sign Out” box.
Clearly, for one to sign OUT, one must be signed IN!
There just does not seem to be any hope that any WSJ staffers employ circulation code writers, or AI which can fix this ages-old incongruity!!!

reviews.title: Scammers
reviews.text: They are literally scamming people on survey apps to download their app and then not paying them.

reviews.title: Automatically plays sound & video!?!!
reviews.text: Invasive, frustrating and disrespectful of surroundings. Can’t find control. Limits the utility of the app to simply READ the WSJ.

reviews.title: No comment(s)
reviews.text: Absolutely ridiculous that the WSJ app does not provide the ability to read or write comments. For this reason, I never use the app; I use a browser instead.The app is useless to me.

reviews.title: Still not working offine
reviews.text:
Two years later and still not fixed. Download editions only to get a no connection error when trying to read an article on a plane with no WiFi. 
Disable the download function until you finally fix it. Stop giving me false hope. 

Downloaded several print versions to read on a flight and did not load when not connected to the internet   After the disastrous update last year, you would think that would have learned how to build a well functioning app.

reviews.title: Ads on paid subscription
reviews.text: Despite paying for a subscription, the app is still showing ads.

reviews.title: Auto-play with sound intrusive
reviews.text: I am no longer able to read at night due to the regular auto playing of video with sound on as it regularly wakes my partner.

reviews.title: Plays ads at full volume
reviews.text: The app started playing ad videos at full volume while scrolling through the front page. Absolutely unacceptable.

reviews.title: Auto-plays videos with sound
reviews.text: The latest version started auto playing videos with sound. There is no way to disable this. You'll be scrolling and all of a sudden a loud video will start playing.

reviews.title: Automatically plays audio!?!
reviews.text:
Still!!!! Ok, I suppose the fact that this has been going on for months means it’s permanent. 

This obnoxious app is totally useless. It randomly starts automatically playing audio at full volume while you’re scrolling — wherever you happen to be at the time you are using it!!! There is no setting to disable this. You can try to silence the outrageous, full-volume audio that randomly begins blaring from your phone by tapping the mute, but it will just automatically unmute itself and do it to you again sometime soon. So, if you, like me, need to be able to control when your phone is going to broadcast audio to the public around you, this garbage app is not for you.

reviews.title: Paid but still get ads
reviews.text: I paid for the subscription (very expensive btw), and I’m still served ads? What kind of dystopian dark pattern is this. Not cool

reviews.title: Ruined “market data” tab
reviews.text: They ruined the “market data” tab, have to swipe a million times get from SPY to Crude, it’s worse than tinder. It’s no longer data, just more articles.

reviews.title: Automatic Video
reviews.text: I hate how video begins playing automatically when I scroll down the list of articles. This is super obnoxious, especially if I happen to put my finger on the video (for scrolling purposes), as this turns off the mute and turns on the volume. I would prefer the videos be segregated entirely in a media section or only available if I open an article.

reviews.title: Horrendous
reviews.text: This app absolutely sucks. I can’t log into this garbage app because both Apple and the tech idiots who created this app suck. Legit signed up via Apple, paid my subscription via Apple and now can’t sign in via Apple like I should. Makes me go through some typical garbage log in process and I’m stuck with a white screen.

reviews.title: Subscription charged as in-app purchases
reviews.text: Beware! There is no way to cancel the subscription. It doesn’t show up in my subscription list in Apple and there is no way to cancel on the WSJ site. Once the promotional price ends, you pay almost as much per month as you do for a year.

reviews.title: Too many mobile ads make for poor user experience
reviews.text: I detest how almost every page on this app includes an ad. It reduces the reading text by a third and makes it very distracting. I can’t count the times I quit reading because of these ads.

reviews.title: New typeface on print edition is terrible
reviews.text: The new sans serif typeface on the home page of the print edition is too light and very hard to read. Looks great until you try to read it. If you have glasses or you’re over 50, good luck. The serif font on the individual stories is fine.

reviews.title: Autoplay videos super annoying
reviews.text: The great reporting etc etc is being ruined by the awful autoplay videos that blast out sound randomly and can’t be turned off in any settings. PLEASE FIX this.

reviews.title: Audio for articles is ruined
reviews.text: This app used to be great. But now if you stay to listen to an article (read by AI) the article will stop if you lock the screen. Or if you navigate away from the app. This ruins the whole reason to use the audio, so you don’t have to stare at the screen. No longer can you lock the phone and put it in your pocket to listen to an article like you can with any of the hundreds of other similar apps. New York Times app can do this, too complicated for you to program, WSJ?

reviews.title: Turn off video autoplay and turn down ad sensitivity
reviews.text: Turn off video autoplay and turn down ad sensitivity

reviews.title: great content, awful app
reviews.text: The audio read option is awesome, great articles, easy access, but has a glaring flaw: settings. For those of us who logon to READ the WSJ, we do NOT want to have a video automatically play. I absolutely HATE auto video. It's distracting from the READING an article. Why can't WSJ make this a setting that can be turned off like 99.9% of other content apps???

reviews.title: Turn off the autoplay
reviews.text: You gotta turn off the video auto play with sound. It’s obnoxious. Especially when your phone is on silent. Turn it off.

reviews.title: Ads playing
reviews.text:
Had wsj for years. Somewhat recently, maybe months or so, the ads have started to automatically play with sound. It's so abrupt and jarring, and plays noise publicly, I'm about to uninstall and unsubscribe. 

Even without sound, for over a year, the auto play has been pausing whatever I'm listening to in the background automatically. Put a setting in to turn it off.

reviews.title: “Restore Purchase”
reviews.text: Since the price hike ($45 ☠️), the app won’t let you read any news articles unless you subscribe or restore purchase. I’ve been loyal to this company for years and have resubscribed. It still won’t let me view any news - just takes me back to the screen to “restore purchase”. If this isn’t fixed within the week, I’m going to delete WSJ and move on to some other news source.

reviews.title: Ads too touch sensitive!
reviews.text: Your overly touch sensitive ads make reading articles in the app an exercise in frustration. Tone down the sensitivity to match your competitors please. I don’t like constantly popping up new ad windows which take me outside your app involuntarily.

reviews.title: Fixes needed
reviews.text:
Love the WSJ., but please fix the audio player for articles!The first 10 seconds it reads some miscellaneous info about the article which can be skipped — and it doesn’t even pronounce things like “WSJ.Magazine” right, which it should.
And second, you can’t even exit the app or lock your iphone while listening to an article. This is very unfortunate

reviews.title: Popup ads? I’m already paying!
reviews.text:
Not sure why I get popup ads in the middle of articles now. Quite annoying. The app is also laggy, which is silly, since all it needs to do is display text. 

That aside, enjoy the articles.

reviews.title: Canceling is a pain
reviews.text: Honesty this has been the hardest cancelation I’ve ever had to deal with. There is no button to cancel subscription. You must call customer service with faulty phone numbers and then they are no help when you get them. I have been trying to cancel for a hour. Honestly ridiculous that I have to go this far just to cancel.

reviews.title: Not free, like it says
reviews.text: No, you have to subscribe unless you just want to read previews.

reviews.title: Opt out bug
reviews.text: If you don’t choose “accept all” it goes into a terminal holding pattern that requires that I delete the app. Until this is fixed, I have to use the browser for content.

reviews.title: Crossword fan
reviews.text: You broke the crossword with the recent update. The keyboard is not ergonomic on iPad, clues bizarrely jump around when inputting letters and the clue being answered no longer appears as a separate line. Please fix or revert to the previous iteration.

reviews.title: SLOW
reviews.text: This app just keeps hanging up. I don’t know if they’re doing it intentionally to force you to look at ads, but I can’t get through a single article without it hanging up. Updates seem to make no difference, and I’m on fiber, so not a bandwidth issue.

reviews.title: Can’t login with Sign In With Apple
reviews.text: I’ll change this rating once this is fixed, but I’ve subscribed to the app but can’t login with Sign In With Apple! I’ve tried over and over on multiple devices. It takes me to the Safari browser, I select my account, it signs in and stays on a blank page. It doesn’t take me back to the app, and the app stays signed out. I’m extremely frustrated with this!

reviews.title: Please fix the Crossword puzzle!
reviews.text: Not sure what happened, but it’s a mess now. Put it back to the previous iteration…from a few days ago so the iOS keyboard can be used and we can preview letters, words etc. Other aspects of the app are fine.

reviews.title: Crosswords are terrible!
reviews.text:
What have you done to the Crossword section?  In landscape, the print is so tiny I can barely see it.  In portrait, I can’t see across and down clues at the same time.  
My completed puzzles don’t stay in the App so I can’t tell which puzzle I did last.  
Please change it back.

reviews.title: AI Listen not working
reviews.text: If you click to read an article and within the article page, hit play to listen to article, it will play.  However, as soon as phone locks or you turn off the screen, the article stops playing. However, if you hit play in the screen where you can scroll through all the articles, black earphone icon appears on bottom right, and the article does not stop playing even if you turn off the screen. Please fix this bug.

reviews.title: Polymarket partnership
reviews.text: They’re still partnered with polymarket despite their own reporting revealing that they pay influencers to shill them

reviews.title: WSJ App now just a con game
reviews.text: News content is no longer accessible via the iPhone app.  Regardless of an active subscription, every attempt to read beyond the headlines will be met with a screen demanding the purchase of an additional $39 monthly subscription.  There are ample legitimate news options available via iTunes apps.  If you truly need to read WSJ, try a print subscription.

reviews.title: New Format
reviews.text:
Where’s the newspaper? I am about ready to cancel my subscription because I can no longer see the entire newspaper and choose what I want to read. Instead, some powers have decided what’s important for me to see. 

For example, where is the Mansions section? It’s not listed as a section but if I go to the print edition (which is clumsy and difficult to navigate), it is there meaning it must still exist. But it doesn’t show in the list of sections in the new app. 

Please bring back the newspaper format in the main menu bar. You can leave all the other items for those who want you to choose what is important to them.

reviews.title: Poly market ads
reviews.text: Get rid of them. I pay for a subscription, I don’t need to see gambling ads here as well

reviews.title: Print Edition?
reviews.text: Why did Print Edition disappear in your last update?    Please bring it back!

reviews.title: Broken
reviews.text: App won’t load. VPN not the issue. Web version only option until this is fixed.

reviews.title: New updates for watchlist and market are terrible!
reviews.text: Wow, over time the content has become less insightful and market-moving news harder to find, but I’ve stuck with the WSJ purely for the ease of use tracking stocks and market data. Now, with the most recent app update that ease of use is gone! You just took away the one piece of value I still found in the WSJ app. I wish you could get back the news and data focus that you had 20 years ago, that was always what made the WSJ stand out, but now you’re trying (and failing) to be just like everyone else and in doing so giving up your value proposition and one real point of differentiation. I wish this weren’t true.

reviews.title: Bait and switch
reviews.text: Beware. If you click on article and can’t access and subscribe, it may charge you for a service that does not include the article or only gives a Barron’s online subscription. Do not buy anything through this app. Customer service does not care and will ignore the issue.

reviews.title: Great reporting, app doesn’t qualify.
reviews.text: I miss the old app, where it read like a newspaper.  I am a baby boomer and  still remember what that was like.

reviews.title: APP needs serious work
reviews.text:
Content top notch, but the app is serious bad.
1. When I open an article, even if the content has been downloaded before, without internet connection it still refuses to load.  This is terrible - internet connectivity should not affect article viewing for the articles that were already downloaded. 
2. Offline mode is buggy.  Today is May 10, 2026.  When I am on a subway, the app reverts all the content back to May 03. 2026.  That means the app is not capable of storing the most up to date version of the content.
3. Comments are not available, this is not that big of a deal but it shows how outdated the technology is.  It should be trivial to have this.

All of this means the tech team is likely making a decision to prioritize serving advertisement, preventing fraud.  The tech team should focus on delighting loyal customer like me, that just want a seamless reading experience regardless of internet connectivity.

reviews.title: What does it take to get it right?!!
reviews.text: Once again, there is a problem with the left column displaying on an IPad.  This is an ongoing problem that has been going on for some time now.

reviews.title: WSJ is great, but app sucks.
reviews.text: So the WSJ is a fantastic news organization, with exceptional journalism. However, their app doesn’t even load anymore. It just sits at the WSJ loading screen and does nothing. I can’t believe I actually pay for this.

reviews.title: AI writing What’s News column again
reviews.text: Get a high school intern to write the what’s News column and maybe it will be intelligible

reviews.title: No BTC ticker?
reviews.text: No bitcoin ticker at the top

reviews.title: A journal is lost quality in terms of providing information. It’s way too common repetitive assignin
reviews.text: Far from the quality, it was too full of passwords and repetitiveness reassigning membership definitely lost quality and a member for well over 50 years used to be quality in issue and function two stuck out reassuring and password

reviews.title: Audio button is annoying
reviews.text: I wish there was a way to disable the audio button. I keep accidentally pressing it.

reviews.title: I'm paying $22.90 for Marketwatch and another $5.95 for the WSJ. That's very expensive!
reviews.text: Why do i need two different subscriptions?   I thought i was getting both + IBD + Barons!  Please contact me!!

reviews.title: Power drain
reviews.text: The WSJ content is terrific, but the app is terrible. It makes my phone hot and quickly drains the battery. They need to fix the app so that it works like it used to

reviews.title: Less Wall Street News, More useless news
reviews.text: They write more on non-business and noise than on what’s actually business news

reviews.title: Absolute nightmare to manage subscription
reviews.text:
I made the mistake of using the apple email forwarding functionality and it broke the WSJ completely. Unable to log in correctly, unable to read content I’ve paid for, and unable to transfer to my normal email. Support is non existent unless you call them. Their support chat is basically a redirect function to other links within the same page. Will not spend another month of subscription on this garbage.

Deleting my account is also near impossible. They hide behind their privacy policies. Sure I guess it’s legal but scummy.

reviews.title: Keeps asking me to subscribe
reviews.text: I’ve been paying for a subscription but it only shows me free content a couple of times then only shows me a subscribe screen. I’ve synced the subscription multiple times but doesn’t work. Ive deleted the app and reinstalled… nothing. I’ve reached out to customer support multiple times, no response. App is a joke at this point and they are taking my money and showing zero content. Now trying to get a refund. Guess what, no reply.

reviews.title: App works okay but music always pauses when i open the app
reviews.text: App works okay but music always pauses when i open the app. Idk why WSJ feels the need to hijack the audio every single time when theres literally nothing playing

reviews.title: Everything is paywalled
reviews.text: Unless you’re paying for this a subscription, don’t even bother. Paywalls are around every corner and renders this app useless. Just include a subscription as part of the download price at this point lol

reviews.title: Broken or just odd
reviews.text: Seems WSJ keeps tinkering with the app. I normally prefer reading the paper using the print edition tab. Now for some odd reason, the Whats New section seems to be written by a poorly trained ai model. Useless and clearly doesn’t match what’s on the actual print edition. Please fix.

reviews.title: Poor functionality
reviews.text: Video pops up on the app and stops the audio that I’m listening to in the Wall Street Journal as well as other applications. Makes me not want to open the app anymore.

reviews.title: Wtf clickbait garbage
reviews.text: Not a serious source of news

reviews.title: App is not functional
reviews.text: Subscription via Apple and every time I access an article it forces me to login again without giving me access to the article. The app is non-functional

reviews.title: Sucks now
reviews.text:
Since they changed the display to a small screen
With a photo of the paper above it. Stupid.

reviews.title: WSJ fails journalism
reviews.text: WSJ owner abdicates journalism to political demons, choosing to offer multiple angles on well-worn Epstein releases rather than pursuing coverage of on-going economic and political fraud… sell out, sell-out!

reviews.title: Doesn’t open anymore
reviews.text:
The digital version on the WSJ used to be a pleasure to use. The months long “improvement” process has resulted in significant slowing of the app as well as bizarre relocations of search functions back and forth across the page. Now, it simply won’t work. I have deleted and reinstalled the app but it remains nonfunctional. Fortunately, I still have the traditional newspaper. Addendum: so the app now works again but still has very frustrating features. For example, when it opens, it displays the previous day’s edition, not the current one. Second, it remains very slow to open page 1 (tho possibly not AS slow as it was). Articles are opening more consistently-previously, you could try to open an article and it would just freeze-that seems better. Fact remains, what was a smooth running, reliable and pleasurable experience has been significantly degraded. They keep talking about “improving” the product but if they were serious, they would go back to square one.

Addendum:
They’re at it again, fiddling with the app and making it extremely frustrating to use-it freezes, cuts out and slows to a crawl. After reboots, shut downs and restarts it reverts to the older version of the app which works flawlessly. You think there’s a lesson in that? Very disappointing.
